card.name: Linking words before electrolyte or muscle-injury risks
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as "of", "or", "in", "as" or "with" that come right before a predicted adverse-effect term. These terms are usually hyperkalemia, hypomagnesemia, myopathy, rhabdomyolysis or hypotension, in warnings about potassium, magnesium or statin interactions.

modes.label: Risk-of linking words
modes.description: The word "of", "in" or "as" after "risk", "result" or "such", just before a named adverse condition.
modes.example: Concomitant use may increase the risk<< of>> hyperkalemia [see Warnings

modes.label: Or between paired conditions
modes.description: The word "or" joining two related lab or muscle conditions.
modes.example: who have a history of hypokalemia<< or>> hypomagnesemia, also monitor

modes.label: Section-number gaps
modes.description: A space or digit inside a cross-reference such as (2.3) after a potassium-monitoring instruction.
modes.example: Measure serum potassium before starting eplerenone tablets and periodically thereafter. (<< >>2.3 ) 2.1

card.writes: No clear output effect; the promoted and suppressed tokens look like unrelated noise.
card.plain: It fires on little linking words just before the text names a potassium, magnesium or muscle-damage problem.
